newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi sees March CPI below 2.4 percent.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi sees March CPI below 2.4 percent.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Saturday that Italian consumer price inflation would fall to below 2.4 percent year-on-year in March despite an increase in the price of cars, the news agency ANSA reported.

It said Prodi made the forecast at a meeting of businessmen and trades unionists in the northern city of Brescia. Inflation rose 2.4 percent year-on-year in February and preliminary March figures from 11 sample cities are due on March 20 and 21.
"In the month of March we will be below that figure even though there has been a rise in the list prices of cars," Prodi told the meeting, organised by employers' group Confindustria.
Several automobile companies raised prices this month. FIAT, the domestic market leader, added 1.6 percent to its list prices from March 3.
Italian inflation has fallen steadily over the past year and stood at 4.5 percent year-on-year in March 1996. Prodi's government has set a 1997 average inflation target of 2.5 percent.
The national statistics institute Istat is scheduled to release official CPI data for March on April 7.
